[LLM] UAT-8302 NetDraft persistence scheduled task (Appunion.exe under \ProgramData\Microsoft\Microsoft\) Installation High
Hunts for the schtasks.exe invocation NetDraft uses to gain reboot persistence after initial implantation. The task name impersonates Microsoft\Windows\Maps with a hard-coded UUID-like string and points at C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Microsoft\Appunion.exe — both signatures are specific to this UAT-8302 / LongNosedGoblin tradecraft and not produced by any legitimate Windows component. Rationale: The persistence command is quoted verbatim in the Talos report (`schtasks /create /ru system /tn Microsoft\Windows\Maps\{a086ff1e-d6dc-45f7-b3e4-6udknw82sa} /tr 'C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Microsoft\Appunion.exe' /F`). The double `Microsoft\Microsoft\` directory and the malformed-GUID task name are unique fingerprints — no legitimate Windows installer creates that path. ESET's LongNosedGoblin write-up confirms NosyDoor uses scheduled-task persistence in the same cluster. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-8302/ • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/longnosedgoblin-tries-sniff-out-governmental-affairs-southeast-asia-japan/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/china-linked-uat-8302-targets.html
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1036.005 T1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/create"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "Appunion.exe",
    @"\ProgramData\Microsoft\Microsoft\",
    "a086ff1e-d6dc-45f7-b3e4-6udknw82sa")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has @"Microsoft\Windows\Maps\" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\{[a-f0-9\-]{30,}\}")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProc = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          IsRemoteSession = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has "/create"
| where CommandLine has_any (
    "Appunion.exe",
    @"\ProgramData\Microsoft\Microsoft\",
    "a086ff1e-d6dc-45f7-b3e4-6udknw82sa")
   or (CommandLine has @"Microsoft\Windows\Maps\" and CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\{[a-f0-9\-]{30,}\}")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType
title: UAT-8302 NetDraft Scheduled Task Persistence (Appunion.exe)
id: 2c8a4f71-3b1a-4c8f-9d7e-1d1f7a83a402
description: Detects scheduled task creation matching the NetDraft/NosyDoor persistence pattern used by UAT-8302 / LongNosedGoblin — schtasks.exe creating a task under Microsoft\Windows\Maps\{GUID-like} that executes C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Microsoft\Appunion.exe.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-8302/
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/longnosedgoblin-tries-sniff-out-governmental-affairs-southeast-asia-japan/

detection:

  selection_str:

ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=schtasks.exe Processes.process="*/create*" (Processes.process="*Appunion.exe*" OR Processes.process="*\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Microsoft\\*" OR Processes.process="*a086ff1e-d6dc-45f7-b3e4-6udknw82sa*" OR Processes.process="*Microsoft\\Windows\\Maps\\{*}*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

[LLM] UAT-8302 whatpc.ps1 host-recon script and ReconLiteDebug/RunWhatPC scheduled tasks Reconnaissance High
Hunts for the actor's bespoke recon harness: a PowerShell file `whatpc.ps1` dropped to C:\Windows\Temp and persisted via scheduled tasks named ReconLiteDebug or RunWhatPC. The script and task names are unique to UAT-8302 operations and surface in process telemetry whether the binary runs interactively or via schtasks. Rationale: Talos quotes the exact invocations: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -File C:\Windows\Temp\whatpc.ps1` and `schtasks /create /tn 'ReconLiteDebug' ...` / `schtasks /create /tn 'RunWhatPC' ...`. These three strings are unique to UAT-8302's recon harness — `whatpc.ps1` does not match any common red-team or sysadmin tooling, and the task names are observed across multiple intrusions in the same cluster. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-8302/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/china-linked-uat-8302-targets.html
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1053.005 T1082 T1087.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let recon_strings = dynamic(["whatpc.ps1", "ReconLiteDebug", "RunWhatPC"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (recon_strings)
   or (FileName =~ "schtasks.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has @"c:\windows\temp\run.bat" and ProcessCommandLine has "/ru SYSTEM")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          IsRemote = AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
let recon_strings = dynamic(["whatpc.ps1", "ReconLiteDebug", "RunWhatPC"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has_any (recon_strings)
   or (NewProcessName endswith @"\schtasks.exe" and CommandLine has @"\windows\temp\run.bat" and CommandLine has "/ru SYSTEM")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine

[LLM] CloudSorcerer v3 mspdb60.dll side-load via Yandex.exe / VMtools.exe with -r -p:*.ini -s: command line Installation High
Hunts the UAT-8302 CloudSorcerer v3 sideload triad: a benign-named launcher (Yandex.exe or VMtools.exe) executed with the unique flag pattern `-r -p:<file>.ini -s:<n>` that side-loads a hijacked mspdb60.dll which decrypts the .ini-encoded shellcode. The combination of binary name, distinctive cmdline, and mspdb60.dll image-load is not produced by any legitimate Yandex or VMware product. Rationale: Talos directly quotes the loader invocations `Yandex.exe -r -p:test.ini -s:12` and `VMtools.exe -r -p:VM.ini -s:12` and names mspdb60.dll as the malicious side-loaded DLL that decrypts the .ini-encoded CloudSorcerer v3 shellcode. The flag pattern `-r -p:*.ini -s:<digit>` is bespoke to this loader (legitimate Yandex Browser / VMware Tools binaries do not accept these arguments) and pairing it with mspdb60.dll loaded from a non-system path makes false positives extremely rare. Cross-checked against Kaspersky's original CloudSorcerer disclosure and the EastWind campaign analysis, which document the same sideload-triad TTP with renamed signed binaries. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-8302/ • https://securelist.com/cloudsorcerer-new-apt-cloud-actor/113056/ • https://securelist.com/eastwind-apt-campaign/113345/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cloudsorcerer-hackers-abuse-cloud-services-to-steal-russian-govt-data/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1027.013 T1055
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// Stage 1 — distinctive launcher cmdline pattern
let sideload_procs = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName in~ ("Yandex.exe", "VMtools.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s-r\s+-p:\S+\.ini\s+-s:\d+"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName,
              FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
              ProcessCommandLine, ProcessId;
// Stage 2 — mspdb60.dll image-loaded by the same process (DLL hijack confirmation)
let hijack_loads = DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "mspdb60.dll"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Yandex.exe","VMtools.exe")
    | project LoadTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, ProcessId = InitiatingProcessId,
              LoadedDll = FolderPath, DllSHA256 = SHA256;
sideload_procs
| join kind=inner hijack_loads on DeviceId, ProcessId
| where LoadTime between (Timestamp .. Timestamp + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          ProcessCommandLine, LoadedDll, DllSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Sentinel cannot observe image-loads without Sysmon, so we anchor on the
// distinctive launcher cmdline pattern alone (rare enough to alert on).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\Yandex.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\VMtools.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s-r\s+-p:\S+\.ini\s+-s:\d+"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: CloudSorcerer v3 mspdb60.dll Side-Load by Yandex.exe / VMtools.exe

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-0994")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-0994")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve

    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities

    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve

Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/

CloudZ RAT potentially steals OTP messages using Pheno plugin

Cisco Talos
2026-05-05 9 use cases 6 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Cisco Talos discovered an intrusion, active since at least January 2026, where an unknown attacker implanted a CloudZ remote access tool (RAT) and a previously undocumented plugin called “Pheno.”

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — CloudZ RAT potentially steals OTP messages using Pheno plugin
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] CloudZ persistence: regasm.exe executing dropped .txt loader (update.txt/msupdate.txt) · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] CloudZ C2/staging beacon: hellohiall.workers.dev or 185.196.10.136:8089 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Pheno plugin recon artefacts: phonelink-<HOST>.txt in Microsoft\feedback\cm staging
[LLM] CloudZ persistence: regasm.exe executing dropped .txt loader (update.txt/msupdate.txt) Installation High
Hunts the SystemWindowsApis scheduled-task persistence chain where regasm.exe is invoked with /nologo and a path to update.txt or msupdate.txt under C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windo(s)Doc\. regasm.exe legitimately consumes .dll/.exe assemblies — pointing it at a .txt file is uniquely characteristic of CloudZ's loader. Rationale: Article quotes the exact persistence pattern: schtasks runs `regasm.exe /nologo <path>\update.txt` from the SystemWindowsApis task. Regasm-with-text-file is a near-impossible legitimate pattern, making this a low-FP alert. Drop paths and filenames lifted directly from the Talos write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/cloudz-pheno-infostealer/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cloudz-malware-abuses-microsoft-phone-link-to-steal-sms-and-otps/ • https://cyberinsider.com/cloudz-malware-hijacks-microsoft-phone-link-to-intercept-sms-and-otps/
ATT&CKT1218.009 T1053.005 T1036.008
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "regasm.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("update.txt", "msupdate.txt")
   or ProcessCommandLine has @"\ProgramData\Microsoft\WindowsDoc\"
   or ProcessCommandLine has @"\ProgramData\Microsoft\windosDoc\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          IsRemoteSession = InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\regasm.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("update.txt", "msupdate.txt")
   or CommandLine has @"\ProgramData\Microsoft\WindowsDoc\"
   or CommandLine has @"\ProgramData\Microsoft\windosDoc\"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName

id: 9a4d5b2c-7e21-4a3b-b6f1-7c4e91f8a2d1
description: Detects the CloudZ RAT persistence chain where regasm.exe is invoked against a .txt file under C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windo(s)Doc\. Regasm legitimately registers .NET assemblies (.dll/.exe) — pointing it at a .txt file is uniquely characteristic of this loader.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/cloudz-pheno-infostealer/

[LLM] Pheno plugin recon artefacts: phonelink-<HOST>.txt in Microsoft\feedback\cm staging Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the Pheno plugin's reconnaissance artefacts: creation of pheno.exe under C:\Windows\TEMP and/or output files named phonelink-<COMPUTERNAME>.txt under C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\feedback\cm or %TEMP%\Microsoft\feedback\cm. Also flags processes scanning for the Phone Link SQLite database (PhoneExperiences-*.db). Rationale: Article specifies the exact filename template `phonelink-<COMPUTERNAME>.txt`, the two staging folders (`C:\programdata\Microsoft\feedback\cm` and `%TEMP%\Microsoft\feedback\cm`), the Pheno binary drop path `C:\Windows\TEMP\pheno.exe`, and the plugin staging dir `C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\whealth\`. None of these paths are used by Microsoft's legitimate Phone Link product. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/cloudz-pheno-infostealer/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cloudz-malware-abuses-microsoft-phone-link-to-steal-sms-and-otps/ • https://www.csoonline.com/article/4167092/stealthy-malware-abuses-microsoft-phone-link-to-siphon-sms-otps-from-enterprise-pcs.html
ATT&CKT1005 T1119 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let pheno_files = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
    | where (FileName =~ "pheno.exe")
         or (FileName startswith "phonelink-" and FileName endswith ".txt"
             and FolderPath has @"\Microsoft\feedback\cm\")
         or (FolderPath has @"\ProgramData\Microsoft\whealth\")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath,
              SHA256, Initiator = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitiatorCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              Account = InitiatingProcessAccountName;
let phonelink_db_access = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName startswith "PhoneExperiences-" and FileName endswith ".db"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("PhoneExperienceHost.exe","YourPhone.exe","PhoneLink.exe",
                                            "svchost.exe","explorer.exe","backgroundtaskhost.exe",
                                            "runtimebroker.exe","searchindexer.exe")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath,
              Initiator = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitiatorCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              Account = InitiatingProcessAccountName;
union pheno_files, phonelink_db_access
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where (TargetFileName =~ "pheno.exe")
     or (TargetFileName startswith "phonelink-" and TargetFileName endswith ".txt"
         and TargetFilePath has @"\Microsoft\feedback\cm\")
     or (TargetFilePath has @"\ProgramData\Microsoft\whealth\")
     or (TargetFileName startswith "PhoneExperiences-" and TargetFileName endswith ".db"
         and ActingProcessName !in~ ("PhoneExperienceHost.exe","YourPhone.exe","PhoneLink.exe",
                                     "svchost.exe","explorer.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername

[LLM] CloudZ C2/staging beacon: hellohiall.workers.dev or 185.196.10.136:8089 Command & Control High
Hunts CloudZ RAT C2 and staging traffic — direct egress to 185.196.10.136 on TCP/8089 (decrypted secondary-config C2) and HTTP(S) to any *.hellohiall.workers.dev Cloudflare Workers subdomain (calm-wildflower-1349, round-cherry-4418, orange-cell-1353 observed; pattern is wildcard). Rationale: Direct C2 IP/port (185.196.10.136:8089) and the operator-owned `*.hellohiall.workers.dev` Cloudflare Workers domain are dedicated CloudZ infrastructure called out in the article and confirmed in the BleepingComputer/CyberInsider write-ups. Wildcard subdomain match catches future rotations under the same handle (HELLOHIALL). Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/cloudz-pheno-infostealer/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cloudz-malware-abuses-microsoft-phone-link-to-steal-sms-and-otps/ • https://cyberinsider.com/cloudz-malware-hijacks-microsoft-phone-link-to-intercept-sms-and-otps/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1571
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (RemoteIP == "185.196.10.136" and RemotePort == 8089)
     or (RemoteUrl endswith ".hellohiall.workers.dev")
     or (RemoteUrl in~ ("calm-wildflower-1349.hellohiall.workers.dev",
                        "round-cherry-4418.hellohiall.workers.dev",
                        "orange-cell-1353.hellohiall.workers.dev"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol,
          Initiator = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatorCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatorPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          Account = InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  ( CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where (DestinationIP == "185.196.10.136" and DestinationPort == 8089)
         or RequestURL has ".hellohiall.workers.dev"
         or DestinationHostName endswith ".hellohiall.workers.dev"
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceUserName,
              DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DestinationHostName,
              RequestURL, DeviceAction ),
  ( ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where (DstIpAddr == "185.196.10.136" and DstPortNumber == 8089)
         or DstHostname endswith ".hellohiall.workers.dev"
         or Url has ".hellohiall.workers.dev"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername,
              DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, DstHostname, Url, DvcAction ),
  ( DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name endswith ".hellohiall.workers.dev"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCodeName )

description: Egress to the CloudZ RAT C2 IP 185.196.10.136 on TCP/8089 or to any *.hellohiall.workers.dev Cloudflare Workers subdomain used by the operator (handle HELLOHIALL).

author: SOC Detection Engineering

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] ScarCruft sqgame supply-chain delivery domain contact (BirdCall/RokRAT)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — A rigged game: ScarCruft compromises gaming platform in a supply-chain attack
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] BirdCall trojanized APK/mono.dll SHA1 match on Windows endpoints · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] BirdCall RokRAT cloud-storage C2 beacon (Dropbox/pCloud) from non-browser process · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] ScarCruft sqgame supply-chain delivery domain contact (BirdCall/RokRAT) Delivery High
Hunts for Windows endpoint or DNS contact with the trojanized Yanbian gaming platform domains (sqgame.net, sqgame.com.cn, xiazai.sqgame.com.cn) which delivered the BirdCall/RokRAT backdoor via a malicious mono.dll update package. Any contact from a managed host warrants investigation as the article confirms the update channel was malicious from late 2024. Rationale: sqgame.net, sqgame.com.cn and xiazai.sqgame.com.cn are explicitly identified by ESET as the supply-chain delivery domains. Any contact is high-fidelity since these are not general-purpose services outside Yanbian-region gamers. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0067/ • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/rigged-game-scarcruft-compromises-gaming-platform-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1071.001

[LLM] BirdCall trojanized APK/mono.dll SHA1 match on Windows endpoints Installation High
Alerts on the exact ESET-confirmed SHA1 hashes of the BirdCall-trojanized Yanbian gaming APKs (ybht.apk, sqybhs.apk) appearing on Windows endpoints, or on file events touching the malicious mono.dll update artefact (xiazai.sqgame.com.cn/dating/20240429.zip). Catches enterprise-managed analyst workstations or BYO-laptop sync that pulled the malicious payload. Rationale: Both SHA1 hashes (03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF and FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9) and the filenames ybht.apk, sqybhs.apk, 20240429.zip are explicitly listed in ESET's IOC table and code blocks. Hash-based file detection has near-zero FP outside of analyst sample handling. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0067/ • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/rigged-game-scarcruft-compromises-gaming-platform-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1204.002

let BadNames = dynamic(["ybht.apk","sqybhs.apk","20240429.zip"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in~ (BadSha1)
   or FileName in~ (BadNames)
   or (FileName =~ "mono.dll" and FolderPath has "sqgame")
   or FileOriginUrl has_any ("sqgame.net","sqgame.com.cn","xiazai.sqgame.com.cn")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] BirdCall RokRAT cloud-storage C2 beacon (Dropbox/pCloud) from non-browser process Command & Control Medium
Hunts for the BirdCall/RokRAT command-and-control pattern: backdoor processes making API calls to Dropbox or pCloud cloud storage outside of normal browser/sync-client context. ESET explicitly states BirdCall uses Dropbox/pCloud as its primary C2 channel, so non-browser beaconing to api.dropboxapi.com / content.dropboxapi.com / api.pcloud.com from unusual process trees is high-signal. Rationale: ESET explicitly states BirdCall uses Dropbox and pCloud as C2 channels. Pairing the cloud-API destination with a non-browser/non-sync-client process tree is the high-fidelity pivot — bare cloud-API traffic alone is noise. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/ • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/rigged-game-scarcruft-compromises-gaming-platform-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1567.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let CloudC2 = dynamic(["api.dropboxapi.com","content.dropboxapi.com","api.pcloud.com","eapi.pcloud.com","api.pcloud.link"]);
let KnownClients = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","Dropbox.exe","DropboxUpdate.exe","pCloud.exe","OneDrive.exe","explorer.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (CloudC2) or tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host) has_any (CloudC2)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (KnownClients)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize EventCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Urls=make_set(RemoteUrl,10) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where EventCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
let CloudC2 = dynamic(["api.dropboxapi.com","content.dropboxapi.com","api.pcloud.com","eapi.pcloud.com","api.pcloud.link"]);
let KnownClients = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","Dropbox.exe","DropboxUpdate.exe","pCloud.exe","OneDrive.exe","explorer.exe"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
    (ImNetworkSession
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
     | where DstHostname has_any (CloudC2) or Url has_any (CloudC2)
     | where ProcessName !in~ (KnownClients)
     | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=SrcUsername, Process=ProcessName, Cmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, Dst=coalesce(DstHostname,Url), Src="ImNetworkSession"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
     | where DestinationHostName has_any (CloudC2) or RequestURL has_any (CloudC2)
     | where isnotempty(SourceHostName)
     | extend Process = tostring(split(DeviceCustomString1, "|")[0])
     | where Process !in~ (KnownClients) or isempty(Process)
     | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, User=SourceUserName, Process, Cmd=RequestURL, Dst=coalesce(DestinationHostName,RequestURL), Src="CommonSecurityLog"))
| summarize EventCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Destinations=make_set(Dst,10) by Host, Process, User
| where EventCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(*dropboxapi.com OR *api.pcloud.com OR *eapi.pcloud.com OR *api.pcloud.link) -@Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\Firefox.exe OR *\\Dropbox.exe OR *\\pCloud.exe OR *\\OneDrive.exe OR *\\explorer.exe)

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9") or SHA1 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9") or MD5 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9") or SHA1 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9") or MD5 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Shai-Hulud npm preinstall: node spawns Bun runtime from bun-dl-* tmpdir Installation High
Detects the Shai-Hulud worm's signature execution chain where the malicious npm preinstall hook (node setup.mjs) downloads the Bun JavaScript runtime to a mkdtempSync-created directory prefixed bun-dl- and then executes execution.js under Bun to evade EDRs that only watch for node children of npm install. Targets the exact loader behaviour in setup.mjs (SHA256 4066781f...) shared across mbt@1.2.48 and the three compromised @cap-js packages. Rationale: Pivots on the exact mkdtempSync prefix 'bun-dl-' and the platform-specific Bun release-asset names (bun-windows-x64-baseline, bun-linux-x64-baseline, bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline, bun-linux-aarch64, bun-darwin) hard-coded in setup.mjs (SHA256 4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34), plus the literal 'execution.js' filename — the article calls out 'a different binary name that bypasses' EDR monitors of node children, which is the exact behaviour this UC flips back into a detection. IOCs taken directly from StepSecurity's runtime trace.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1027.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where (FileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
      or FolderPath has "bun-dl-"
      or FolderPath has "bun-windows-x64-baseline"
      or FolderPath has "bun-linux-x64-baseline"
      or FolderPath has "bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline"
      or FolderPath has "bun-linux-aarch64"
      or FolderPath has "bun-darwin"
      or ProcessCommandLine has "execution.js")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","preinstall","npm install","yarn install","pnpm install")
   or FolderPath has "bun-dl-"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where TargetProcessName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun-dl-","bun-windows-x64-baseline","bun-linux-x64-baseline","bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline","bun-linux-aarch64","bun-darwin","execution.js")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","preinstall","npm install","yarn install","pnpm install")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has "bun-dl-"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Shai-Hulud AI coding-agent persistence: .claude/settings.json + .vscode/tasks.json drops Installation High
Detects the Shai-Hulud worm's novel persistence mechanism where the payload commits or writes .claude/settings.json (abusing Claude Code's SessionStart hook) and .vscode/tasks.json (with runOn:folderOpen) into every accessible repository. Any developer re-opening the repo in VSCode or Claude Code silently re-executes the malware — this is one of the first supply-chain campaigns weaponising AI-agent config files. Rationale: The article describes 'one of the first supply chain attacks to target AI coding agent configurations as a persistence and propagation vector', specifically dropping .claude/settings.json (SessionStart hook abuse) and .vscode/tasks.json with runOn:folderOpen. Detection bucket-aggregates both filenames in a 1h window because the loader writes them as a pair, and falls back to the suspect-parent process list (node/bun/git) when only one of the two files is observed — that combination is essentially nil in legitimate developer activity. Sigma omitted because the detection is a multi-file correlation, not a single event.
ATT&CKT1546 T1195.002 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let _window = 1h;
let _suspect_files = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
    | where (FolderPath endswith @"\.claude\settings.json"
          or FolderPath endswith "/.claude/settings.json"
          or FolderPath endswith @"\.vscode\tasks.json"
          or FolderPath endswith "/.vscode/tasks.json")
    | extend FileKind = case(
        FolderPath has ".claude", "claude_settings",
        FolderPath has ".vscode", "vscode_tasks",
        "other")
    | extend Bucket = bin(Timestamp, _window);
_suspect_files
| summarize FilesDropped = make_set(FileKind),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Paths = make_set(FolderPath, 50),
            Initiators = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 20),
            InitiatingCmds = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 20)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, Bucket
| where array_length(FilesDropped) >= 2
   or Initiators has_any ("node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","git.exe","git")
| order by FirstSeen desc
let _window = 1h;
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFilePath endswith @"\.claude\settings.json"
      or TargetFilePath endswith "/.claude/settings.json"
      or TargetFilePath endswith @"\.vscode\tasks.json"
      or TargetFilePath endswith "/.vscode/tasks.json")
| extend FileKind = case(
    TargetFilePath has ".claude", "claude_settings",
    TargetFilePath has ".vscode", "vscode_tasks",
    "other")
| extend Bucket = bin(TimeGenerated, _window)
| summarize FilesDropped = make_set(FileKind),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            Paths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 50),
            Actors = make_set(ActorUsername, 20),
            ActingProcs = make_set(ActingProcessName, 20),
            ActingCmds = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine, 20)
            by DvcHostname, Bucket
| where array_length(FilesDropped) >= 2
   or ActingProcs has_any ("node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","git.exe","git")
| order by FirstSeen desc
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\.claude\\settings.json OR */.claude/settings.json OR *\\.vscode\\tasks.json OR */.vscode/tasks.json) OR @file.path:(*\\.claude\\settings.json OR */.claude/settings.json OR *\\.vscode\\tasks.json OR */.vscode/tasks.json)) (@Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\bun.exe OR *\\git.exe OR */node OR */bun OR */git) OR @process.executable.path:(*\\node.exe OR *\\bun.exe OR *\\git.exe OR */node OR */bun OR */git))

[LLM] Shai-Hulud known-bad setup.mjs / execution.js SHA256 hash match Installation High
Detects on-disk or in-execution presence of the two Shai-Hulud loader/payload files by their byte-identical SHA256 hashes — the setup.mjs loader (4066781f...) is identical across all four confirmed compromised packages (mbt@1.2.48, @cap-js/sqlite@2.2.2, @cap-js/postgres@v2.2.2, @cap-js/db-service@v2.10.1), and execution.js (80a3d287...) is the 11.6 MB obfuscated credential stealer. This is the highest-fidelity retrospective hunt across npm-using hosts and CI runners. Rationale: The article explicitly states setup.mjs is 'SHA-256 (identical across all compromised packages) 4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34' and execution.js for mbt@1.2.48 is 80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac. These are the highest-fidelity IOCs in the campaign — byte-identical across four packages confirms the same operator/toolchain. Union across file, process and image-load tables ensures retrospective coverage whether the artifact landed on disk only, was executed, or was loaded.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let _ShaiHulud_Hashes = dynamic([
    "4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34",  // setup.mjs (loader, identical across all 4 compromised packages)
    "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac"   // execution.js (11.6MB obfuscated payload from mbt@1.2.48)
]);
union isfuzzy=true
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
                  InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType="ProcessCreated", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
                  InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName, Source="DeviceProcessEvents" ),
    ( DeviceImageLoadEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType="ImageLoaded", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine="",
                  InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="DeviceImageLoadEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc
let _ShaiHulud_Hashes = dynamic([
    "4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34",
    "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac"
]);
union isfuzzy=true
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes) or Hash in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath,
                  Hash = coalesce(TargetFileSHA256, Hash), ActingProcessName, ActorUsername,
                  Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType="ProcessCreated",
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  Hash = SHA256, ActingProcessName = ParentProcessName,
                  ActorUsername, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600

| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.

SecurityEvent

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac") or SHA1 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac") or MD5 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac") or SHA1 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac") or MD5 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

elementary-data Compromised on PyPI and GHCR: Forged Release Pushed via GitHub Actions Script Injection

StepSecurity
2026-05-04 11 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A malicious version of elementary-data (0.23.3) was published to PyPI and is, at the time of writing, still listed as the latest release. The same release run also pushed a multi-arch container image to GitHub Container Registry at ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary, tagged both 0.23.3 and latest.

ATT&CKT1021.002 T1190 T1195.002 T1204.002 T1555.003
Domainsigotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Install of trojaned elementary-data 0.23.3 via pip / poetry / uv · [LLM] Docker / Kubernetes pull of compromised ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary image
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Malicious elementary.pth dropped in Python site-packages · Article-specific behavioural hunt — elementary-data Compromised on PyPI and GHCR: Forged Release Pushed via GitHub A
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound to elementary-data exfil C2 igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.sky · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Stage-3 exfil archive trin.tar.gz POST via curl --data-binary · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] Outbound to elementary-data exfil C2 igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.sky Command & Control High
Detects DNS resolution, HTTP/S egress, or proxy traffic to the credential-stealer C2 hard-coded in the trojaned elementary-data 0.23.3 .pth payload. A single hit anywhere in the org indicates a host has installed the compromised PyPI package or pulled the trojaned ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary image and that the stage-3 collector has reached the network. Rationale: Anchored on the single hard-coded exfil host igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud named in the StepSecurity write-up. Any DNS / HTTP egress to this host is unambiguous: the domain has no benign use case and was registered for this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/elementary-data/elementary/issues/2205 • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
let MaliciousDomain = "igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud";
let WindowDays = 30d;
union isfuzzy=true
    (DeviceNetworkEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(WindowDays)
        | where RemoteUrl has MaliciousDomain
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Source = "DeviceNetworkEvents"),
    (DeviceEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(WindowDays)
        | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
        | where AdditionalFields has MaliciousDomain or RemoteUrl has MaliciousDomain
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort = toint(0), Source = "DeviceEvents(DNS)")
| order by Timestamp desc
let MaliciousDomain = "igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud";
let WindowDays = 30d;
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImDnsActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where DnsQuery has MaliciousDomain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, SrcHost = SrcHostname, SrcIP = SrcIpAddr, Indicator = DnsQuery, Source = "ImDnsActivity"),
    (DnsEvents
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where Name has MaliciousDomain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, SrcHost = Computer, SrcIP = ClientIP, Indicator = Name, Source = "DnsEvents"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where DestinationHostName has MaliciousDomain or RequestURL has MaliciousDomain or DestinationDnsDomain has MaliciousDomain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, SrcHost = SourceHostName, SrcIP = SourceIP, Indicator = coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain), Source = "CommonSecurityLog"),
    (Syslog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where SyslogMessage has MaliciousDomain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, SrcHost = HostName, SrcIP = HostIP, Indicator = SyslogMessage, Source = "Syslog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Malicious elementary.pth dropped in Python site-packages Installation High
Detects creation of the trojaned `elementary.pth` loader inside any Python site-packages directory. Legitimate elementary-data releases ship no top-level .pth file; this file is unique to 0.23.3 and is what triggers payload execution on every Python interpreter startup. Rationale: The article confirms `elementary.pth` is the single malicious artifact added in 0.23.3 vs 0.23.2 and that no legitimate elementary release ships a .pth file — making the filename in site-packages a near-zero-FP signal. Size gate of 50KB further separates the ~245KB base64 payload from any legit user-created .pth. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/elementary-data/elementary/issues/2205 • https://pypi.org/project/elementary-data/
ATT&CKT1546 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where FileName =~ "elementary.pth"
| where FolderPath has_any ("\\site-packages\\", "/site-packages/", "/dist-packages/")
| extend IsOversized = (FileSize > 50000)  // legit .pth files are <1KB; payload is ~245KB
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, IsOversized,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where TargetFileName =~ "elementary.pth"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\site-packages\\", "/site-packages/", "/dist-packages/")
| extend IsOversized = (TargetFileSize > 50000)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, IsOversized, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Install of trojaned elementary-data 0.23.3 via pip / poetry / uv Delivery High
Detects any package manager invocation requesting the malicious pinned version `elementary-data==0.23.3` (or the unpinned `latest`/`>=0.23.3` form that PyPI still resolves to the trojaned release at the time of the StepSecurity report). Catches the install moment so the host can be quarantined before the .pth fires on next interpreter startup. Rationale: Article names the exact poisoned version (0.23.3) and the package canonical names (`elementary-data` / `elementary_data`). Process-create with these two strings in the command line is high-fidelity because no benign install would target a known-malicious pinned version after the StepSecurity disclosure. Cross-checked against: • https://pypi.org/project/elementary-data/#history • https://github.com/elementary-data/elementary/issues/2205

   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip.exe", "pip3.exe", "poetry.exe", "uv.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "elementary-data"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("==0.23.3", " 0.23.3", "elementary_data-0.23.3", "elementary-data-0.23.3")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "elementary-data" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("install", "add", "sync") and not(ProcessCommandLine has "==0.23.4" or ProcessCommandLine has "<0.23.3"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
    (SecurityEvent

        | where CommandLine has_any ("==0.23.3", " 0.23.3", "elementary_data-0.23.3", "elementary-data-0.23.3")
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName),

        | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "elementary-data" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "elementary-data"

[LLM] Docker / Kubernetes pull of compromised ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary image Delivery High
Detects docker, containerd, podman, crictl, kubectl, or kubelet pulls of the trojaned GHCR image — including the dangerous unpinned `:latest` form that resolved to the malicious digest sha256:31ecc5939de6...634255 between 2026-04-24 and the cleanup. Fires on the pull itself rather than at runtime so deployments can be blocked before the container ever runs the .pth payload. Rationale: Anchored on the exact registry path called out in the article (`ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary`) and the known-bad digest prefix (`sha256:31ecc5939de6...634255`). Catches both Docker CLI users and Kubernetes admission for image creates — the article specifically warns that `:latest` resolved to the trojaned image for every team that didn't pin by digest. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/elementary-data/elementary/pkgs/container/elementary • https://github.com/elementary-data/elementary/issues/2205
ATT&CKT1610 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("docker.exe", "docker", "podman.exe", "podman", "crictl.exe", "crictl", "kubectl.exe", "kubectl", "nerdctl.exe", "nerdctl", "buildah", "skopeo")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary"
| extend IsLatestOrBad = ProcessCommandLine has_any (":latest", ":0.23.3", "sha256:31ecc5939de6") or not(ProcessCommandLine matches regex @":(0\.23\.[4-9]|0\.2[4-9]|[1-9])")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, IsLatestOrBad
| order by Timestamp desc
let TargetImage = "ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary";
union isfuzzy=true
    (SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where EventID == 4688
        | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\docker.exe", "\\podman.exe", "\\crictl.exe", "\\kubectl.exe", "\\nerdctl.exe")
        | where CommandLine has TargetImage
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, Source = "SecurityEvent4688"),
    (ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where TargetProcessName has_any ("docker", "podman", "crictl", "kubectl", "nerdctl", "buildah", "skopeo")
        | where TargetProcessCommandLine has TargetImage
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername, NewProcessName = TargetProcessName, CommandLine = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate"),
    (Syslog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where ProcessName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "kubelet", "crio")
        | where SyslogMessage has TargetImage
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = "", NewProcessName = ProcessName, CommandLine = SyslogMessage, Source = "Syslog"),
    (AKSAudit
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where Verb in ("create", "update", "patch")
        | where ObjectRef has "pods" or ObjectRef has "deployments" or ObjectRef has "statefulsets" or ObjectRef has "daemonsets" or ObjectRef has "cronjobs"
        | where RequestObject has TargetImage
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer = tostring(parse_json(tostring(User)).username), Account = Username, NewProcessName = Verb, CommandLine = tostring(RequestObject), Source = "AKSAudit")
| extend IsLatestOrBad = CommandLine has_any (":latest", ":0.23.3", "sha256:31ecc5939de6") or not(CommandLine matches regex @":(0\.23\.[4-9]|0\.2[4-9]|[1-9])")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
